raw_case_text:
A 68-year-old female, a resident of Karnal (Haryana, North India), a known case of diabetes mellitus (for 5 years on diet control), and chronic liver disease (for 3 years) presented with complaints of cough, generalized weakness, and significant weight loss since one month. The cough was insidious in onset, dry in nature, and not associated with any aggravating or relieving factor. She was diagnosed with chronic liver disease 3 years ago and an evaluation was done earlier for the same and was found to be cryptogenic in origin. There were no similar complaints among her family members. On examination, she was thin built and pale. The patient was afebrile and haemodynamically stable. There were no palpable lymph nodes. Systemic examination was unremarkable.
Initial blood investigations revealed anaemia (haemoglobin 10.2 g/dl), total leucocyte count 12x109 cells/l, platelet count 150x109 cells/l, erythrocyte sedimentation rate 59 mm/hour and differential count was neutrophil 41%, lymphoctes 27% and eosinophils 32%. Mean corpuscular volume and mean corpuscular haemoglobin concentration were 84 fL and 32 g/dl, respectively. Peripheral blood smear showed normocytic normochromic anaemia with eosinophilia (figure 1). Absolute eosinophil count was 4x109 cells/l. Hepatic functions were normal except for hypoalbuminemia (2.78 g/dl). Renal function tests were normal. ELISA for HIV-1 and HIV-2, anti-hepatitis C antibody, hepatitis B surface antigen were negative. Reaction to the tubercular skin test was less than 10 mm. Chest radiograph showed increased bronchovascular markings with right hilar prominence (figure 2). Stool samples tested two times but did not reveal any ova or parasite. Ultrasound abdomen showed coarse liver echotexture. During the course of hospital stay, the patient continued to have a dry cough and generalized weakness. The patient was given deworming measures (albendazole and diethylcarbamazine). Repeat blood counts revealed persistent eosinophilia. Test for echinococcus serology was negative. Anti-filarial antibodies were negative. Tests for anti-nuclear and anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies were negative. Echocardiography was normal with no evidence of vegetation. A contrast-enhanced CT of the thorax and abdomen was done, which revealed enlarged non-necrotic mediastinal lymph nodes with features suggestive of chronic liver disease. Microscopic examination of needle-aspirated bone marrow and biopsy examination revealed increased eosinophilic precursors with no abnormal cells. Endoscopic bronchial ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration of mediastinal lymph nodes was consistent with tubercular inflammation with acid-fast stain positive for bacilli. Acid-fast bacilli culture grew Mycobacterium tuberculosis over a period of 3 weeks in the BACTEC medium. The patient was started on anti-tubercular treatment (isoniazid, rifampicin, ethambutol, and pyrazinamide) and her eosinophil counts gradually returned to normal levels with in 1 week.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 68-year-old female presented with dry cough, generalized weakness, and significant weight loss for one month.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 68-year-old female presented with an insidious, non-productive cough, progressive generalized weakness, and significant weight loss over a 1-month period. The cough was non-paroxysmal without aggravating or relieving factors. She had a history of diet-controlled diabetes mellitus and cryptogenic chronic liver disease.
subjective.past_medical_history: Diabetes mellitus for 5 years on diet control; chronic liver disease of cryptogenic origin for 3 years. Resident of Haryana, North India. No family history of similar complaints.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for persistent dry cough, generalized weakness, and weight loss. Negative for fever, hemoptysis, or dyspnea. Home medications (diet-controlled) and allergies not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Thin built, pale, afebrile, hemodynamically stable. No palpable peripheral lymphadenopathy. Systemic examination unremarkable.
objective.routine_investigations: Hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL, MCV 84 fL, MCHC 32 g/dL, total leukocyte count 12 x 109 cells/L (neutrophils 41%, lymphocytes 27%, eosinophils 32%), absolute eosinophil count 4 x 109 cells/L, platelets 150 x 109 cells/L, ESR 59 mm/hr. Peripheral smear: normocytic normochromic anemia with marked hypereosinophilia. Serum albumin 2.78 g/dL; liver and renal function tests normal. HIV-1/2 ELISA, anti-HCV, and HBsAg negative. Tuberculin skin test induration <10 mm. Stool examinations (x2) negative for ova/parasites. Serology for Echinococcus, anti-filarial antibodies, ANA, and ANCA negative. Echocardiography normal without vegetations. Abdominal ultrasound: coarse liver echotexture. Chest X-ray: increased bronchovascular markings with right hilar prominence. Empirical deworming with albendazole and diethylcarbamazine yielded no change in eosinophilia.
objective.advanced_workup: Contrast-enhanced CT thorax and abdomen: enlarged non-necrotic mediastinal lymph nodes and changes of chronic liver disease. Bone marrow aspirate and trephine biopsy: increased eosinophilic precursors without dysplastic or neoplastic cells. Endobronchial ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) of mediastinal lymph nodes performed.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis: Mediastinal tuberculous lymphadenitis presenting with marked peripheral hypereosinophilia and leukemoid reaction, confirmed by EBUS-guided fine-needle aspiration of mediastinal lymph nodes demonstrating granulomatous inflammation with acid-fast bacilli (AFB) on stain and mycobacterial culture growing Mycobacterium tuberculosis in BACTEC medium at 3 weeks. Parasitic infections, allergic conditions, hypereosinophilic syndrome, and hematological malignancies were ruled out. Management & Outcome: Prescribed 4-drug antitubercular therapy (isoniazid, rifampicin, ethambutol, pyrazinamide). Peripheral eosinophil counts completely normalized within 1 week of therapy, accompanied by resolution of cough and constitutional symptoms.
